G2_out_of_distribution.note: characterization not pass/fail: does the coverage guarantee transfer to a NEVER-SEEN organism?

MONDRIAN_class_conditional_fix.note: per-class threshold so the ESSENTIAL target class is covered at 1-alpha in-dist; OOD essential coverage = does the class-conditional guarantee TRANSFER to a novel organism?

scope: n=2 organisms (demonstration/bound, not a population estimate); conservation features; essentiality prediction; in-silico; characterizes the ABSTENTION guarantee under organism shift, not a target
verdict: G1 PASS (marginal conformal calibrated: in-dist marginal coverage 0.901 ~ target 0.90). FINDING 1 (the caution): MARGINAL conformal is VACUOUS for the targets — its 90% coverage is entirely the ~93% non-essential majority (non-ess coverage 0.9753/0.9851); the ESSENTIAL class is covered 0.0 in-dist / 0.0 OOD (essentially never). A marginal coverage guarantee does NOT make abstention trustworthy for the actual targets. FINDING 2 (the fix + its transfer): MONDRIAN class-conditional conformal restores essential-class coverage to 0.9375 in-dist (by construction) at a mean set size 1.24; the honest OOD result — does the class-conditional guarantee TRANSFER to a never-seen organism — is M. tb essential coverage 0.5457 (DEGRADES <0.85, gap +0.392; set size 1.0615). Honest bound: trustworthy target-class abstention needs class-conditional conformal, and even then its guarantee on a novel organism is not fully preserved.
